newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - U.S. debt vols soft before jobs data.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - U.S. debt vols soft before jobs data.

text.p: Implied volatilities for U.S. debt options were flat to weaker Thursday as the underlying futures firmed.
Options traders called the softness in volatility somewhat surprising coming on the eve of a U.S. employment report. April jobs data will be released Friday.

Both June and September bond volatility levels remained under 9.0 percent, a historically low measure, traders said. June closed at 8.58 percent, down from a session high of 8.70 percent, but slightly higher than Wednesday's settlement of 8.50 percent.
September bond volatility ended at 8.94 percent, down from 9.12 percent the previous session.

Floor traders said some analysts Thursday appeared to be scaling back their predictions for April nonfarm payrolls growth, which could help explain the weakness in volatility. Economists polled earlier in the week predicted a gain of 211,000 for non-farm payrolls.
"Volatility is telling you the market is expecting a smaller move rather than a larger move" in futures after the jobs numbers are released, said one bond options trader.
